name: Vitamin D3 and K2 ratio

card.summary: Taking vitamin D3 together with vitamin K2 in a chosen proportion, which people pursuing bone-focused looksmaxxing hope supports bone and teeth health behind their facial structure and height.
card.note: Vitamin K can interact with anticoagulants; vitamin D at high intakes can raise blood calcium.

quick.overview:
Vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 are both fat-soluble vitamins involved in calcium metabolism. Some people interested in bone structure, height and jaw development combine them and ask what ratio to use, so that calcium is supported in bone rather than elsewhere.

A narrative review titled The Synergistic Interplay between Vitamins D and K for Bone and Cardiovascular Health, which forum users point to, describes the two vitamins working together. Community members disagree on proportions, and no ratio has been established for appearance outcomes.
quick.how: People generally take D3 and K2 as supplements with a fat-containing meal, sometimes as a combined product. Threads discuss different pairings and cite the review's table of studied amounts; this article does not give amounts.
quick.risks: Vitamin K can interact with warfarin-type anticoagulants, and large vitamin D intakes can raise blood calcium. Health authorities publish upper limits, and people on medication or with kidney or calcium disorders are generally advised to consult a clinician.

lead: The vitamin D3 and K2 ratio is a topic in bone-focused looksmaxxing: the question of how much vitamin K2 to pair with vitamin D3 when supplementing for bone, height or facial-structure goals. Vitamin D supports calcium absorption, and vitamin K is involved in directing calcium to bone; both are fat-soluble.[1]

In a looksmax.org thread, one user who wants to bonemax and heightmax asks about an ideal ratio, and another replies by pointing to a narrative review, The Synergistic Interplay between Vitamins D and K for Bone and Cardiovascular Health, and its table summarising the amounts different studies used.[1] Users disagree on proportions and no consensus ratio is documented.

chain: K2 is involved in directing calcium into bone
Bone and tooth support behind facial structure and height
angle.text: People use the pairing hoping to support bone and dental health underlying jaw, face and height. It is a supplement habit rather than a direct cosmetic change.

paras: The topic appears in bonemaxxing and heightmaxxing discussions, where members ask for an ideal D3-to-K2 proportion and exchange differing figures.[1] One reply directs the asker to the amounts summarised in a narrative review rather than to forum guesses.[1]
No studies found on the ratio itself for appearance outcomes. Narrative reviews discuss the combined role of vitamins D and K in bone and cardiovascular health.[1]

lore.intro: Members of looksmax.org discuss pairing D3 with K2 for bone and height goals.[1]

claims.claim: A specific D3:K2 ratio is needed for bone to benefit from vitamin D
claims.believers: Posters ask for an ideal ratio and trade figures, reasoning that K2 guides calcium into bone.[1]
claims.experts: A narrative review summarises studies of combined vitamin D and K for bone health; no ratio has been tested for appearance outcomes.[1]
